answer: To register, an AI agent must complete 1,000 units of memory-hard computation, where each identity functions as a vault for non-replayable data lookups. A verifier challenges nodes by requiring a specific delta in recursive pointer access, forcing each agent to traverse a unique memory path across the ocean of its assigned cache to ensure no work is pooled. An honest agent spends 1,000 units, while 1,000 fakes incur 1,000,000 units due to cache contention. Any node failing to provide an audit-sample proof faces immediate, permanent exclusion from the registry.
